title: Metric Vanishing Act — post-incident notes
content:
Summary:

Short version: On 2025-11-02 22:17 UTC we received a cascade of SLO-burn and downstream error-rate alerts caused primarily by a sudden loss of a set of high-cardinality metrics (app.request_latency_bucket*, cache.hit_ratio per-host) from our instrumentation pipeline. Dashboards showed 'flatlines' (zero series) for multiple important series; SLOs spiked because the request_latency histogram stopped reporting. The incident lasted ~2 hours for full recovery, with partial mitigation at +25m.

Why this doc: working scratchpad for hypotheses, triage commands, quick mitigations, and next-actions. Not a polished postmortem yet — this is the on-call/early post-incident record.

Observed symptoms (timeline highlights):
- 2025-11-02 22:15 UTC — first PagerDuty alert: SLO (webapi.p95) breach.
- 22:16 — multiple engineers see 0 series in prometheus for metric app.request_latency_bucket_total and cache.hit_ratio{host=*}. Grafana panels returned "no data" (not zero).
- 22:20 — alert flood; many dependent alerts (service-latency, perf-regressions) fired due to missing histogram-based metrics.
- 22:40 — noticed Prometheus remote_write queue length spike and throttling logs in cortex-writer-01.
- 22:50 — rolling restart of exporter-configured-hosts temporarily restored traffic for some hosts.
- 00:20 UTC — full ingestion resumed after bumping remote_write concurrent shards and reverting a config change in the exporter (partial change rolled back).

Initial hypotheses (ordered by likelihood at the time):
1) Upstream exporter config change introduced a label set growth (new label "region_code") causing cardinality explosion -> write backpressure -> remote_write dropped the series.
2) Prometheus scrape job misconfiguration (changed scrape interval to 0s or disabled target) -> missing scrapes -> data absent.
3) Remote-write component (Cortex/Thanos) had shard-saturation or compaction backlog that returned 429s -> Prometheus dropped samples and reported 'dropped samples due to queue full'.
4) Downstream assembler (ingest pipeline) had an outage/GC pause causing series ingestion to be delayed/missed.
5) Alerting rule evaluation bug that treats missing series as 0 (we verified this is not the case; our rules use absent() checks).

Useful checks to run (promql / kubectl / logs) — copy/paste friendly:
- Check target scrape health:
  up{job="node-exporter"}  # look for 0 or "down"
  up{job="app-instrumentation"}  # verify targets present

- Detect sudden series count changes:
  count({__name__=~"app_request_latency_bucket.*"}) by (job)
  count_series() - increase over last 1h, or run: count({job=~".*app.*"})

- Prometheus remote_write queue metrics (example):
  prometheus_remote_storage_queue_length
  prometheus_remote_storage_dropped_samples_total
  prometheus_tsdb_head_series

- Look for 429/503 from remote write in Prometheus logs:
  kubectl -n monitoring logs prometheus-main-0 | grep -E "remote write|429|throttl|queue full|dropped"

- Check Cortex/Thanos writer metrics:
  cortex_remote_write_queue_length  # if present
  cortex_http_response_codes_total{code="429"}

- Quick exporterd checks on hosts:
  kubectl -n platform logs deployment/app-exporter -c exporter | tail -n 200 | grep -i "labels"
  curl http://app-exporter.service/metrics | head -n 200 | grep -E "region_code|cache.hit_ratio|request_latency"

Immediate mitigations applied during incident (notes):
- 22:28 — applied global silence for dependent symptom alerts (not SLO targets) to reduce pager noise; left SLO-owner PD rota intact.
- 22:32 — disabled non-critical high-cardinality instrumentation temporarily via a flag rollout on exporter (feature-flagged) to reduce cardinality while we triaged.
- 22:40 — increased remote_write concurrent shards on cortex-writer group (size from 4 -> 8) which lowered queue_length and reduced dropped_samples.
- 22:55 — reverted an accidental new-label rollout (region_code) via the config-service rollback PR (#4217) which stopped new high-cardinality series from appearing.

Root cause (synthesis):
A recent config rollout to the app exporter (deployed at 22:12 by a metrics infra change) added a free-form label (region_code) inadvertently populated with host-specific values for some hosts. This dramatically increased cardinality for certain histograms. The influx of new series caused Prometheus -> remote_write queues to fill, resulting in sample drops and series being absent from the query engine for downstream evaluation. The remote-write component (Cortex writer cluster) partially degraded under the load (429s) which amplified the missing-data effect.

Contributing factors:
- No automated pre-release cardinality safety check for new exporter labels.
- Remote-write queue metrics existed but critical thresholds were not wired to a runbook/action.
- Alert rules for missing-series were not specific enough (alerted many dependent rules instead of the root missing-metrics symptom first).
- Silence and mitigation steps were manual and scattered across Slack / PD.

What went well:
- We had a feature-flag in exporter config allowing quick disable of the new label emission. That allowed a fast partial mitigation.
- Observability telemetry (queue_length, dropped_samples) helped identify remote_write saturation.
- On-call team coordinated escalations and engaged metrics infra quickly.

What we missed / improvements:
- Lack of pre-deploy guardrails for metric label changes. Need automated checks in CI to detect label cardinality changes or free-form label additions.
- Missing a "missing-series" primary alert that points directly to metric ingestion issues (presently rules cascade).
- No cookbooked action for remote_write 429 spikes — we manually guessed increasing shards would help.
- Prometheus disk/TSDB head metrics aren't monitored aggressively; had they been, we would have seen head_series growth earlier.

Runbook (draft) — triage order for future similar incidents:
1) Confirm symptom: Are multiple series missing or is it target-specific? Run: count({__name__=~"app_request_latency_bucket.*"}) by (instance, job)
2) Check Prometheus logs for dropped samples and remote_write errors (429/queue full).
3) Inspect remote_write queue metrics (length, oldest sample age, dropped_samples_total). If queue_length > threshold (configurable), consider:
   a) Temporarily increase remote_write concurrency or queue capacity (if safe in cluster).
   b) Apply exporter flag to stop emitting high-cardinality labels.
4) If missing due to disabled scrape targets: check service discovery and scrape configs. Re-enable targets or adjust relabel.
5) If root cause is new label emission: rollback exporter config and redeploy.
6) Silence dependent alerts, keep root-metric alert open and page SRE lead.
7) Communicate in incident channel with short summary and ETA for next update.
8) After recovery, capture a snapshot of prometheus TSDB/remote_write metrics for postmortem.

PromQL alerts to implement (proposals):
- Metric ingestion health (fires early):
  expr: increase(prometheus_remote_storage_dropped_samples_total[10m]) > 0
  note: pages SRE and alerts only the ingestion-owner, not all dependents.

- Sudden series growth detector (pre-deploy safety):
  expr: (count({job="app-instrumentation"}) - count_over_time({job="app-instrumentation"}[1h])) / count_over_time({job="app-instrumentation"}[1h]) > 0.5
  note: used in CI to compare metrics from canary vs baseline.

- High-cardinality label gating (CI job idea):
  - Run prometheus-style label cardinality scan on exported metrics in PR, fail if new labels have > N unique values (N configurable).

Action items (owners assigned):
- [Ava] Create CI check prototype that scans new exporter config and fails PRs that add free-form labels (due 2026-03-01).
- [Samir] Implement a dedicated 'ingestion-health' alert with narrow routing to metrics-infra rotation (due 2026-02-28).
- [Lina] Add runbook steps for safe remote_write shard scaling and test in staging (due 2026-03-10).
- [Devon] Document exporter feature-flag patterns and safe rollback play (due 2026-03-05).
- [Priya] Postmortem writeup draft with timeline, RCA, and follow-ups (due 2026-02-20).

Open questions / unsettled items:
- We increased remote_write concurrency during incident — what is the long-term cost/impact? Need capacity planning for cortex write nodes.
- Is there a way to enforce a global policy that prevents free-form labels from being merged into exporter config?
- How to avoid alert fatigue when multiple dependent alerts fire because of a single ingestion failure? (hypothesis: route dependent alerts to 'informational' during ingestion fault).

Notes / links to artifacts created during the incident:
- Rollback PR: github.com/redwood/metrics-configs/pull/4217
- Temporary silence on PD: PD-SILENCE-20251102-1
- Logs snapshot: s3://incidents/2025-11-02/metrics-logs.tar.gz
- Temporary Grafana snapshot: https://grafana.redwood.com/d/abc123/metric-vanish?orgId=1

Final thought (tl;dr): missing metrics incidents almost always look like downstream service failures but are often caused by upstream label/cardinality changes or ingestion throttling. Low-friction, testable pre-deploy checks for labels combined with a focused ingestion-health alert would drastically shorten time-to-detect and reduce pager cascades.

-- end of scratchpad --
summary: Early post-incident notes for missing-series incident caused by unintended high-cardinality label rollout; includes triage commands, immediate mitigations, runbook draft, and action items.
